title: Tabnas structured diagnostic
description: The JSON shape emitted when a TabnasError is serialized: TS JSON.stringify(err) (via toJSON) and Go json.Marshal(err) (via MarshalJSON). Only `code` is contractual across runtimes; message, hint and src are informative text and not in parity (see DIVERGENCE.md 'Not divergences'). `expected` is an over-approximation of what could have matched. `len` counts Unicode code points OF THE TOKEN SOURCE, so its string-unit arithmetic never diverges between runtimes; the two lexers once cut different token SPANS for bad tokens, which made len/pos/col differ on those paths even for pure-ASCII input — repaired, and both ports now position a string error on the offending construct. `col` carries the recorded astral-character divergence: TypeScript counts UTF-16 units, Go counts runes (DIVERGENCE.md 'Column positions for astral characters'). `pos` is NOT in that class — see its own description.

status.description: Always 'failure': a diagnostic is only emitted for a failed parse.

code.description: The error code (e.g. 'unexpected', 'unterminated_string'). THE ONLY CROSS-RUNTIME-CONTRACTUAL FIELD: fixtures pin codes, and the base codes are listed in AGENTS.md 'Error codes'.

message.description: The one-line rendered message (TS txts().msg, Go Detail) — NOT the multi-line frame that Error.message / Error() renders. Informative text, not in cross-runtime parity.

hint.description: The hint text, trimmed, without the 2-space display indent the rendered frame uses. Informative text, not in cross-runtime parity. Optional: a degenerate error (TS errdesc failure path) can lose it.

row.description: 1-based row (line) of the failing token. For rows containing astral characters before the error, column arithmetic differs per runtime (see top-level description).

col.description: 1-based column of the failing token. TypeScript counts UTF-16 units, Go counts runes — divergent only when astral characters precede the token on its line.

pos.description: 0-based source position of the failing token. TypeScript counts UTF-16 units; Go counts BYTES. This is NOT the same class as col: col agrees throughout the BMP and diverges only above it, while pos diverges for every character above U+007F. Measured with a non-ASCII character before the failure point — for the two-byte U+00E9, TS reports pos 4 and Go 5; for the three-byte U+20AC, TS 4 and Go 6. Do not compare pos across runtimes on input that is not pure ASCII. An earlier version of this schema said Go counted runes, which told a BMP-only consumer that pos was safe when it is not.

len.description: Length of the failing token's source text in Unicode code points (deliberately NOT UTF-16 units), so the counting unit never diverges between runtimes. The token SPAN itself once differed where the lexers cut bad tokens differently; that is repaired, and both ports now span the offending construct. 0 when there is no token source.

rule.description: The failing rule's name; '' when only the no-rule sentinel was available.

ruleStack.description: Rule names root-first, including the failing rule as the last entry; sentinel (no-rule) entries are skipped. Empty when the failure happened outside any rule.

token.description: The token the parse failed on.

expected.description: Tokens some alternate of the failing rule names at this position (lookahead position 0 for the rule's current state), deduplicated and sorted ascending. An over-approximation — conditions/counters may still reject them; empty means no token constraint was recorded, not that nothing can match.

src.description: The full source LINE containing the error (line `row` of the source, trailing carriage return stripped); '' when the row is invalid or the source is unavailable. Informative text, not in cross-runtime parity.

plugins.description: Names of all registered plugins in registration order. Deliberately a list, not a single 'plugin' field: the engine cannot honestly attribute an error code to one package.

version.description: The engine version (equals the package version of the runtime that produced the diagnostic).
